data.name: Parashurama
data.gender_notes: Parashurama is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Parashurama was an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. He was born to Rishi Jamadagni and his wife Renuka, as a vow fulfilled by their son. Famed for his bravery, he wielded an axe and destroyed the Kshatriya rulers 21 times to restore the balance between the Kshatriyas and the Brahmins. The name Parashurama carries the meaning “Rama with axe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Parashurama usually hope their child will grow to embody rama with axe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of bravery and balance in Hindu mythology.
data.etymology: Parashurama belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rama with axe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parashurama total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Parashurama is a legendary warrior-hero in Hindu mythology, who is revered for his martial prowess and dedication to righteousness. He is also known as the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu and belongs to the lineage of sage Jamadagni. Parashurama is celebrated for having avenged his father's death and maintaining the balance between the powers of the Kshatriyas (ruling class) and the Brahmins (priests) by eliminating 21 unjust rulers. His story forms an integral part of Hindu epics and has significantly influenced Indian art, literature, and folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: Parashurama's story holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism and reinforces the importance of righteousness, respect for Just Authority, commitment to dharma, and the power of vows. It illustrates Lord Vishnu's role in governing the universe through his avatars and the significance of selfless acts to restore balance and order (Rta). Parashurama's story also underscores the idea of ahimsa (non-violence) and gradually transforming one's nature from violent to peaceful - a concept known as Parashurama Maharshi. Additionally, Parashurama was one of the first teachers of the ancient Hindu martial art "Kalaripayattu," which uses supracalcular yoga for flexibility, strength, concentration, and enhancing spiritual awareness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parashurama, meaning 'Rama with the axe', embodies the warrior spirit and destructive force within us. He represents the fierce determination to protect dharma and eliminate evil, symbolized by his axe. His life story inspires us to face challenges courageously and transform adversity into strength.

historical_references.reference: Parashurama is considered an incarnation of Vishnu, and is the sixth avatar in Hindu mythology. He is also known as Rama with the axe or Rama the destroyer. This avatar is said to have appeared around 3100 BCE to 2900 BCE and is believed to have destroyed the Kshatriya warrior class, which had become corrupt and violent.
historical_references.context: He is considered an incarnation of Vishnu and is believed to have destroyed the corrupt and violent Kshatriya warrior class.

historical_references.reference: Parashurama is also known for his role in the Mahabharata epic, where he is said to have appeared around 3000 BCE. In the epic, Parashurama is requested by Krishna to create new kings to rule over the earth after the destruction of the Kuru dynasty in the great battle of Kurukshetra. Parashurama creates 21 new kings, each ruled over one province of the earth.
historical_references.context: He is requested by Krishna to create new kings and creates 21 new rulers to rule over the earth.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern context, the name Parashurama is popularly known for its association with martial arts training, mythology, and gaming. Parashurama is a legendary warrior and sage from Hindu mythology, who is considered the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu. This name is frequently referenced in various cultural contexts, especially in Indian folklore and literature. In terms of modern trends, Parashurama's name is commonly seen on three major platforms: TV shows and movies, web comics and manga, and video games. In TV shows and movies, Parashurama's story is often retold with modern adaptations and interpretations. For instance, the Indian mythological series 'Chakravartin Ashoka Samrat' features Parashurama as a main character. In web comics and manga, Parashurama is depicted as a powerful warrior and teacher, often showcasing his mastery of martial arts. One popular example is the webcomic 'Parashurama: The Tale of a Warrior God', which chronicles Parashurama's life and adventures. Lastly, in video games, Parashurama is a commonly used character name or reference. For example, in the game 'God of War', Kratos' son Atreus is named after Parashurama, and in the game 'Smite', Parashurama is a playable god. Overall, Parashurama's name continues to resonate in modern culture through various adaptations and interpretations across different media platforms.
